Le conflit de 11 jours qui a fait rage e: The 11-day conflict between Israel and Palestine left 230 Palestinians (including 65 children) and 12 Israelis dead. The surge in violence sent shockwaves through communities across Canada. In Montréal, there were numerous demonstrations in support of the Palestinian people.
Le premier ministre Justin Trudeau, de s: Prime Minister Justin Trudeau, for his part, <l1>welcomed</l1> the formation of a new Israeli government on June 13, reiterating the “shared values” of the two countries.
Le 28 mai, Ottawa a également investi <l: On May 28, Ottawa also committed <l1>$25 million</l1> to support Palestinian populations.
Pour les Palestiniens du Canada, ces der: For Palestinians in Canada, these latest statements are not enough. They want Ottawa to acknowledge their suffering and to denounce the close ties between Canada and Israel, which show up in official rhetoric, arms sales and the definition of antisemitism. It is a little-covered subject, and one La Converse has looked into.
« Les 25 millions aux Palestiniens ne si: “The 25 million for Palestinians means nothing if Justin Trudeau keeps selling weapons to the Israeli state,” says Leila*, who preferred not to reveal her identity for security reasons. A kufiya worn proudly over her shoulders, the Canadian-Palestinian activist does not feel defended by Canada.
Elle a le regard déterminé et le ton rev: She has a determined gaze and a tone that demands answers; a need for justice drives her. Leila came to Canada alone in 2017. She has lived in the Middle East, but never in Palestine. Her entire family was expelled from Jerusalem and Jaffa in 1948.
« J’y suis “retournée” grâce à mon passe: “I ‘returned’ there a few years ago thanks to my Canadian passport,” she says, torn between gratitude and sadness. “I went to my country of origin with another passport, one from a country that is another colonizer,” she continues bitterly, referring to the situation of First Nations. Since arriving in Canada, she has made it a point of honour to denounce the close ties between Ottawa and Tel Aviv.
À l’ONU, le vote du Canada est systémati: At the UN, Canada systematically votes in favour of Israel. Since 2006, Ottawa has rejected a resolution on the Palestinian people’s right to self-determination 14 times. Justin Trudeau finally voted in favour in November 2019. “All Canadian governments have the same position on the situation in Israel/Palestine. It’s always a disappointing reaction,” says Rafel Silver, a retired social worker involved with the organization Independent Jewish Voices. Jewish and born in the United States, he moved to Israel at 18.
« J’étais jeune, je voulais de l’aventur: “I was young, I wanted adventure and to know my roots,” he says with a touch of romanticism. He served in the army for two years. Little by little, disillusionment set in. “I was sent everywhere: to Gaza, to the West Bank… I saw how Palestinians were treated every day. I didn’t want to raise my children there,” he says. After living in Israel for 17 years, he immigrated to Canada for work and feels “extremely grateful” to have been able to settle here in 2001.
Pour lui, il est crucial de montrer que: For him, it is crucial to show that “the Canadian Jewish community is not monolithic.” “People are waking up and starting to ask questions about how Palestinians are treated,” he says with passion. He believes Jews in Canada must speak up to make it known that not all of them support Israel.
Selon Leila et Rafael Silver, c’est la v: According to Leila and Rafael Silver, the problem with the government’s positions is its desire for balance. The use of the word “conflict” to describe the situation is increasingly troubling. “The two sides are not equal. It’s deeper than a conflict, it’s apartheid,” say the two activists. Rafael Silver gets worked up: “Why mention only Israel’s right to live in peace and not that of Palestinians in the statements?”
«Les Palestiniens nous le disent depuis: “Palestinians have been telling us for years, but the word ‘apartheid’ is still used timidly by the media,” says historian Dyala Hamzah.
C’est justement le mot utilisé par Human: It is precisely the word used by Human Rights Watch in a <l1>report</l1> published in April 2021. A few months earlier, the Israeli Jewish organization B’Tselem denounced the same situation of apartheid in a <l2>report</l2>. That an Israeli organization uses the same term shows that “things are starting to creak,” according to the researcher.
Des manifestants qui soutiennent la Pale: Protesters supporting Palestine. Photo: Sandrine Edmee
L’historienne estime que le Canada ne se: The historian believes Canada will not be the first to recognize and denounce the state of apartheid in Israel, as Ottawa has always traditionally supported the Jewish state. There are several reasons for this: among them, U.S. hegemony and Canada’s strong ties with its neighbour, but also the trauma of the Holocaust.
Beaucoup montrent aussi du doigt la défi: Many also point the finger at the definition of antisemitism adopted by Canada. Promoted in 2016 by the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance (IHRA), it is denounced by the Palestinian community, but also by Jews, Israelis and many voices around the world. It is the official definition of G7 countries such as France, Germany and the United States, and also of Quebec since June 9, 2021. “This definition is fraudulent, because it conflates criticism of Israel with antisemitism,” the historian explains. A conflation Rafael Silver knows well.
En raison de son caractère passionné et: Because of his passionate nature and his activism, he is sometimes “called a traitor” by members of his community. “It’s so ridiculous that I burst out laughing. Then I tell them: ‘Walk where I’ve walked, see what I’ve seen and live what I’ve lived to understand what Palestinians go through every day.’” Proud to be Jewish, he speaks bitterly of his service in the Israeli army and of the disillusionment he experienced living there.
Le 13 mai, Jagmeet Singh, chef du Nouvea: On May 13, Jagmeet Singh, leader of the New Democratic Party (NDP), called on Justin Trudeau in a petition to stop selling weapons to the state of Israel. Alexandre Boulerice, the NDP’s deputy leader, wants the same. “The sale of weapons must end, products coming from Israel must be identified and economic pressure must be put on the country,” says the MP, who believes Canada’s <l1>official position</l1> is a good one, but that it is not backed or defended by action. Weapons worth nearly $14 million were sold to Israel in 2019, according to Global Affairs Canada <l2>data</l2>. That is an insignificant amount compared with the $2.9 billion earned from arms sales to Saudi Arabia the same year. Alexandre Boulerice nonetheless points out that the contract with Israel may carry some influence on Canada’s position: “It’s still a contract, which creates jobs.” Canada is far from being the biggest arms seller to the Jewish state.
À ce chapitre, les États-Unis arrivent e: On that front, the United States ranks first, followed by Germany, whose sales account for 70% and 24% respectively of conventional arms imports from 2009 to 2020. Weapons from Canada represent 0.3% of Israeli imports and 0.4% of exports from Ottawa, according to data from the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI). Following the request from Jagmeet Singh and the NDP, Prime Minister Justin Trudeau gave no response. Asked about it, Minister Marc Garneau did not respond to our interview request. Global Affairs Canada spokesperson Grantly Franklin only told us that exports are governed by Canada’s Export and Import Permits Act (EIPA). The law prohibits the sale of weapons to countries that violate human rights, unless they can show that Canadian weapons have not been used against civilians. While this is currently impossible to determine for Israel/Palestine, doubts exist about weapons sold to Saudi Arabia: they are reportedly being used in the war that has ravaged Yemen since 2014, according to a <l1>report</l1> by the UN Group of Eminent Experts on Yemen (GEE).
Lors d’une réunion sur la Palestine, le: At a meeting on Palestine on May 27, the UN Human Rights Council asked states not to sell weapons that would present “a clear risk of being used to commit or facilitate serious violations of international humanitarian law and human rights law.”
Les relations entre le Canada et l’État: Relations between Canada and the state of Israel are not limited to weapons. Well aware of Ottawa’s actions on this front, Leila points to the close ties between the two countries and, above all, the existence of the Canada-Israel Free Trade Agreement (CIFTA). For example, more than $40,000 in aeronautical and space equipment was exported in 2019 and 2020, according to Global Affairs Canada <l1>data</l1>. Other ties between the two countries continue to raise concern. One example is the recruitment of Israeli army (IDF) soldiers on Canadian soil. In October 2020, a <l2>complaint</l2> was sent to the Minister of Justice asking for an investigation into the matter, but Ottawa did not respond to the request, alleging that <l3>it would be up to the police to investigate</l3>.
« Cela se fait contre la loi sur l’enrôl: “It’s done in violation of the Foreign Enlistment Act, but there is an exception for consular officers and Israeli nationals. There’s a legal loophole,” explains Dyala Hamzah. This recruitment is not unique to Canada. It happens more widely in the United States and France, whose nationals make up the vast majority of lone soldiers, the foreign soldiers in the Israeli army. By comparison, Canadians are estimated to represent 3% of the IDF’s foreign-national soldiers, according to data obtained by CBC.
Se pourrait-il que le gouvernement canad: Could the Canadian government be influenced by lobby groups in choosing its positions? In the Canadian Parliament, there is a Canada-Israel Interparliamentary Group (CAIL). It is made up of 59 members from all political stripes, whom we rigorously analyzed to better understand the group. Of them, 24 are Conservative, 16 Liberal, 8 Bloc Québécois and 3 belong to the NDP.
Le Parlement ne finance pas ce genre de: Parliament does not fund this type of group, but provides administrative support, in this case a secretary. Neither the secretary nor the group’s chair, Mount Royal MP Anthony Housefather, answered our questions about CAIL’s activities. It is hard to know what role such a gathering plays. For Dyala Hamzah, its existence helps “forge ties” and strengthen the friendship between the two countries.
Randall Garrison, membre du NPD et du CA: Randall Garrison, an NDP member of CAIL, was offered a trip paid for by the Jewish state. He says the trip helped him in his role within the group, according to an article in La Presse. In 2018, a coalition of hundreds of organizations, elected officials, activists and academics signed an appeal calling for the party’s withdrawal from CAIL.
Questionné au sujet des trois néo-démocr: Asked about the three New Democrats in CAIL, the NDP’s Alexandre Boulerice says we should not “exaggerate the influence of these groups.” “The NDP is a big political movement, and we’re not against the state of Israel either. Its citizens must be able to live in peace. There are different sensibilities within the NDP. I have no problem with colleagues who are members of this group,” he says in defence. For his part, Mr. Boulerice belongs to the Canada-Palestine Parliamentary Friendship Group.
Cela lui a permis de voyager en Israël e: That allowed him to travel to Israel and Palestine from March 30 to April 6, 2018. Does he play a mediating role between Palestinian and Canadian leaders? “We hold more meetings among members in Canada. The idea is to make statements and interventions to defend Palestinians,” Mr. Boulerice explains.
Leila dénonce également l’Université McG: Leila also denounces McGill University for its ties with the state of Israel. Students, teachers, graduates and faculties have signed a petition calling on the administration to stop all investment in Israeli companies and the Jewish state. Among other things, they denounce the funding of Israeli settlements, transport companies and banks. “McGill has never condemned the Canary Mission site, even though many students are on it,” she says, outraged.
Canary Mission est un site qui répertori: Canary Mission is a site that lists and doxxes (discloses personal information about) anyone “promoting hatred” of the United States, Israel and Jews. This blacklist can be used for intimidation, even violence. According to Leila, those listed are mostly Palestinians and activists in the Boycott, Divestment and Sanctions (BDS) movement, which puts nonviolent pressure on the state of Israel. The petition has not yet been sent to the administration, but professor and Vice-Principal (Academic) Christopher Manfredi has published a response, in which he acknowledges the horror of the “violence shaking the Middle East” and its consequences for the Palestinian and Jewish members of the McGill community. The petitioners find this insufficient.
Nous avons posé plusieurs questions au s: We put several questions to the university’s press office about the points raised by the students. Public relations officer Katherine Gombay answered, in a brief paragraph, that the institution “denounces racism and discrimination in all its forms,” recalling McGill’s fundamental values. In the meantime, Palestinians like Leila continue their activism walking on eggshells.
« Les gens ne savent pas à quel point on: “People don’t know how much we’re harassed. I don’t want to be categorized or have people say I’m antisemitic,” she says. That is why she wanted to remain anonymous. Publishing her name could have serious effects on her academic and professional future.
« Tu ne peux pas décider de ton rôle qua: “You can’t decide your role when you’re a Palestinian in the diaspora. My duty is to stand up for my compatriots and to fight,” she says as a matter of course. A duty she will keep fulfilling until her government truly and lastingly helps Palestinians, not just by giving $25 million to populations. *Her first name has been changed to preserve her anonymity.
